title: The Last Train Home
style: Intimate contemporary folk-soul ballad; close, expressive lead vocal with conversational phrasing, acoustic guitar, soft upright piano and restrained bass. Begin sparse and patient, let a warm pulse enter gradually, open the refrain with subtle harmony and dynamic lift without belting; bridge briefly strips back to guitar and voice, final refrain feels quietly hopeful, unhurried instrumental resolution. Organic drums, no forced climax, preserve space between phrases.
lyrics:
[verse]
The platform lights are turning blue
I keep a seat I never use
A paper cup is growing cold
The things I meant to say stay folded

[chorus]
On the last train home tonight
I'll let the empty seat be mine
Not every road has to lead back
Not every heart must follow tracks
I'll watch the windows turn to gold
And learn to let the evening go

[verse]
The streets are names I used to know
Your corner shop is closing slow
I pass the place where we got lost
And smile at what the years have cost

[bridge]
I thought that moving meant goodbye
But there is room for both inside
A little grief, a little grace
I do not have to leave a trace

[chorus]
On the last train home tonight
I'll let the empty seat be mine
Not every road has to lead back
Not every heart must follow tracks
I'll watch the windows turn to gold
And learn to let the evening go
